# Phase 50 implementation plan — evidence-safe security, analysis, and release-support tools

## 1. Purpose and status

- Operation: Revise this plan only; do not implement Phase 50.
- Output: docs/phase-plans/phase-50-slsa-attestation-security-suite-flagship-plan.md.
- Scope: all I13–I22, I24, I26–I28 requirements and Phase 50 delivery; no reductions.
- Status: Implementation-ready plan; Sections 5, 8, 9, 10, and 11 show zero uncovered, duplicate, dangling, malformed, out-of-order, unpaired, or scope-violating task slices. Execution-time failures remain explicit blockers, never scope reductions.
- Lifecycle authority: no commit, merge, tag, push, upload, publish, deploy, version edit, hook, history rewrite, or worktree removal.

| D50-02 | Unsigned provenance is rejected; I16 requires signed Statement v1/SLSA v1 and trusted hosted-builder evidence for Level 3. |

| Missing remediation source | docs/developer/repository-remediation-plan.md is absent here; no requirement is invented from it and no source requirement is reduced. |

## 3. Goals, verified outcomes, exclusions, and inherited invariants

- Goal: fourteen complete capability families, exact required variants, canonical ToolResult, one ToolFn shared by transports, installed wheel/sdist proof, documentation parity, ship-gate evidence, and truthful flagship handoff.
- Excluded: release execution and every lifecycle action barred in Section 1; no web/frontend product work and no Git hooks.
- Invariants: Python 3.12/uv; stdio-only MCP stdout; stderr diagnostics; structured skipped for absent optional engines; recursive [REDACTED]; fixed-cwd argv-only DEVNULL subprocesses; deny-default independent effects; contained no-follow identity-checked atomic writes; unchanged RED tests during GREEN.
- Completion: every claim and required variant has direct same-revision evidence; missing engines/hardware/builders or missed thresholds block completion rather than weaken it.

## 4. Admission and predecessor gate

P50-001 alone owns admission. It requires the accepted Phase 49 close SHA, designated non-main implementation worktree, clean tracked state, Python 3.12, and passing recorded baselines. Missing predecessor evidence, wrong worktree, dirt, or baseline failure stops all behavior-changing tasks without changing scope.

## 6. Shared contracts and cross-phase handoff

| Contract | Owner / consumer rule |
|---|---|
| Result/object identity | base.py Finding/ToolResult/ToolFn; one registered object per family; CLI/MCP only parse, invoke, render. |
| Options | catalog.py ToolSpec/TOOL_SPECS and config.py closed typed keys; unknown/invalid input fails before execution. |
| Effects | permissions.py adds independent source_write/destructive_write; network/download/cache/build/slow/artifact/browser remain deny-default. |
| Process/output | common.py fixed cwd, argv, DEVNULL, sanitized env, timeout/tree kill, bounded recursive redaction. |
| Filesystem | no-follow symlink/junction/reparse containment, identity recheck, sibling temp+flush+atomic replace, recovery proof. |
| Compatibility | Existing five Phase 50 CLI and MCP contracts remain invocable through canonical objects; aliases contain no business logic. |
| Handoff | Every task retains exact evidence and names one successor; integration consumers never mutate producer evidence. |
